ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic вѣжливои (věžlivoi, “experienced, versed”), itself from вѣжливои (věžlivoi, “knower, competent”), from Proto-Slavic *věďa, from *věděti (“to know”). Compare Old Church Slavonic невѣжда (nevěžda, “ignorant”). See also -ливый (-livyj).

Inherited from Old East Slavic вѣникъ (věnikŭ), from Proto-Slavic *věnikъ, from *věnъ (“wreath”) + *-ikъ, details of further origin unclear (possibly from Proto-Indo-European *woh₁y-nos or derived later) but ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁y- (“to twist, wind, weave”).
